name: Bolivia
overview:
Salt Bae-livia, amirite? Okay, we'll stop peppering in puns.

It feels right for Bolivia to carry the name of Simon Bolivar. Of all the South American countries we visited, this was the place where indigenous Andean identity felt most visible and least polished for tourists.

Bolivia is also poor in a way that is difficult to ignore. Infrastructure lags behind its neighbours, child labour showed up more than once in our trip, and Uyuni can feel far removed from the cosmopolitan Latin America of Medellin or Santiago.

Yet the people we met were consistently kind, especially at moments when they had every opportunity not to be. Then the salt flats appear and the entire country turns otherworldly.

Salt of the earth, quite literally.
